movement_source: row 'ROTE (excluding Notable Items)', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's headline ROTE ex Notable Items fell 24bps, from 11.21% in FY24 to 10.97% in FY25 (ev-1, ev-18), corroborated by the pack's "11.0% ROTE ex Notable Items, 24bps to FY24" (ev-14, ev-26). The fall is almost entirely an earnings effect: the ROTE numerator, net profit attributable to owners adjusted for RSP dividends ex Notable Items, fell $140m to $6,966m from $7,106m (ev-16), with net profit ex Notable Items down 2% to $6,972m as higher income and lower impairment charges were "more than offset by higher expenses" (ev-8, ev-9). Average tangible ordinary equity was essentially flat at $63,476m versus $63,415m (+$61m) (ev-17), so the denominator added only ~2bps of drag. On the statutory basis the decline is smaller: statutory ROTE fell 12bps, 11.01% to 10.89% (ev-2), because Notable Item hedging losses narrowed from $123m to $56m (ev-13).

drivers.bank_label: Net profit excluding Notable Items, down 2%
drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: FY24 ROTE 11.21% x earnings growth of -1.97% (numerator $6,966m vs $7,106m, ev-16). Westpac says net profit ex Notable Items of $6,972m fell 2% as "higher operating income and lower credit impairment charges more than offset by higher expenses" (ev-9): expenses +9%/-$972m including $273m restructuring, +6% ex-restructuring on staff costs and UNITE spend; NII +$557m, non-interest income +$144m, impairments +$113m (ev-10, ev-21).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 less Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Derived as total delta -0.24ppt less the earnings effect; includes the interaction term. Average tangible ordinary equity rose only $61m to $63,476m from $63,415m (ev-17) - average ordinary equity $71,544m vs $71,493m (ev-19), with average intangibles falling to $10,586m from $10,758m (ev-20). Retention was minimal at a 75% FY25 payout ratio with the DRP neutralised and buybacks continuing (ev-29, ev-30); weighted average shares fell 2% (ev-7). Westpac does not publish a ROTE decomposition.

notable_items: Notable Items were hedging items only: a $56m post-tax reduction in FY25 versus $123m in FY24 (ev-13, ev-8). These are excluded from the headline ROTE ex Notable Items row but drive the gap to the statutory ROTE movement.

disagreements.topic: ROTE movement FY25 vs FY24: ex-Notable Items vs statutory
disagreements.explanation: The ex-Notable Items row is Westpac's headline shareholder-value measure. The statutory row includes hedging Notable Items, whose drag narrowed from $123m to $56m, halving the apparent decline. Both are printed on results announcement p10.

values: -20 bps (Return on average ordinary equity ex Notable Items, 9.94% to 9.74%)
disagreements.explanation: Return on average ordinary equity is a named variant using untangible equity as denominator; per Westpac's own vocabulary the headline row is ROTE ex Notable Items. Reported as context only (ev-4).

limitations: Westpac publishes no ROTE walk or bridge chart for FY24 to FY25 in either document. Both driver contributions are my own arithmetic derivation from the ROTE numerator and denominator printed on results announcement p58, not a bank decomposition, so both are capped below chart-level confidence.
The equity_effect value bundles the pure denominator effect and the earnings/equity interaction term; the bank does not split these.

The earnings walk on pack p40 (primary, FY24 to FY25, sum check passed) decomposes net profit ex Notable Items of $7,113m to $6,972m, not the RSP-adjusted ROTE numerator of $7,106m to $6,966m. The $7m/$6m RSP dividend adjustments (ev-16) mean the walk's bars explain the earnings effect qualitatively but do not tie exactly to the ROTE numerator.

The bank qualifies the expense increase: excluding the $273m restructuring charge expenses rose 6%, with "Productivity provided a partial offset" (ev-10) - so the gross cost pressure on ROTE is larger than the net 9% line implies.
Pack p31's CET1 walk is a Mar-25 to Sep-25 (half-on-half) framing and was not used for any contribution.

Buyback and DRP evidence (ev-29, ev-30, ev-31) supports the direction of the equity effect qualitatively; the bank does not quantify the buyback's or DRP's impact on average tangible equity or on ROTE.
